text.hero.eyebrow: North Broward, FL / College Track Skills Training
text.hero.lede: Coach Blake Kingsley just spent two seasons on college staffs that won 51 games, two championships, and a trip to March Madness. Now he is in north Broward, building the exact skills college coaches recruit, one player at a time.
text.aud.1: Every college player was once a middle schooler with a habit nobody caught. We catch it now, while it is still easy to fix — feet, balance, both hands — so nothing is capping you at sixteen.
text.aud.2: This is the level where players separate. We build the speed, the strength through contact, and the decisions that turn a rotation player into a starter coaches build around.
text.aud.3: Time to get in front of the right staffs. Coach Blake sat on their side of the recruiting table. He knows what they need to see on your film, he will tell you the truth about the gap, and then he will train you to close it.
text.prog.1: A full evaluation session. No pitch, no pressure. You leave knowing exactly where your player stands and what the ceiling looks like.
text.prog.2: Full session, full attention. Built around the exact three things standing between you and the next level this season.
text.prog.3: Two to four players at a similar level, going at each other. Competitive reps, real defense, nowhere to hide.
text.prog.4: A twelve week block for juniors and seniors who are serious about hearing from college programs. Guided by a coach who was just recruiting at that level.
text.coach.name: Blake Kingsley
text.coach.title: Founder & Head Skills Coach
text.coach.p1: Blake Kingsley spent the last two seasons on college coaching staffs, first with the Moberly Area Greyhounds, who went 25 and 7 and won the NJCAA Region 16 championship, then with Robert Morris, who won the first Horizon League title in program history and went to the NCAA Tournament. Fifty-one wins. Two championships. Two national tournaments.
text.coach.p2: He is not the coach who yells to look intense. He is the one who catches that your left foot is landing early, fixes it, and then tells you exactly what you did right on the very next rep. Players go hard for him because they can tell he is actually watching them, not running a script.
text.coach.p3: He has also been on the other side of the recruiting table, watching film and deciding which high school players were worth a scholarship. That is the perspective he brings to every north Broward family who walks into a session: a straight read on where you are, and a real plan for closing the gap.
text.pb.lede: Tell us the player, the position, and the one thing standing in their way. We build a custom four week workout block, send it to your inbox, and hand you the download right here.
text.ct.lede: Send the form or email directly. You will hear back within one business day with open slots for your area.
text.area.lede: Sessions run at city parks and community courts across these five cities. Each area below gets its own page with the local schools, the courts we use, and what the schedule there actually looks like.

text.fam.body: The Business Profile is in verification. Until it clears we are not printing quotes you cannot go and check for yourself. Ask at your First Look and we will put you in touch with families already training with us.
text.faq.1.a: Players from roughly 11 through 18, from first year middle school through senior year. Younger players get more habit building, older players get more decision work and recruiting support.
text.faq.2.a: City parks and partner courts across north Broward County. When you book, you get the exact location for your area. If you have access to a court through a school or community center, we can often train there.
text.faq.3.q: How fast will we see a difference?
text.faq.3.a: Form changes show up in two to three weeks. Game changes usually take six to eight, because a skill has to survive speed, contact, and fatigue before it shows up on a Friday night.
text.faq.4.q: Do you help with college recruiting?
text.faq.4.a: Yes, inside the College Track Program. Coach Blake spent the last two seasons on college staffs at the NJCAA and NCAA Division I levels, so he has evaluated high school film from the recruiting side. That includes film review, highlight reel guidance, and help building and sending a recruiting profile.
text.faq.5.q: Is the First Look session really free?
text.faq.5.a: Yes. It is a full evaluation. You leave with a written summary of strengths and gaps whether or not you book anything after.
text.faq.6.q: Do you train girls teams and players?
text.faq.6.a: Yes. Every program listed is open to any player. Skill work does not change by gender.
text.coach.h2: He builds the player you are trying to become.

text.mth.h2: Every session runs these five steps.
text.mth.lede: This is how skill gets built so it survives a real game. Each step only works because the one before it is already automatic.
text.mth.1.title: Screen
text.mth.1.body: We watch you move before we change anything. Stance, balance, and the hand you have been hiding.
text.mth.2.title: Isolate
text.mth.2.body: One flaw at a time, slowed down until it is automatic. This is the part most trainers skip.
text.mth.3.title: Load
text.mth.3.body: Add speed, then contact, then fatigue. If it only works fresh, it will not work in March.
text.mth.4.title: Read
text.mth.4.body: Live reps against a defender. Skills become decisions or they never show up on film.
text.mth.5.title: Log
text.mth.5.body: Numbers on paper every session. You will see yourself pulling away before you feel it.
text.nite.h2: Win each practice. Win each day.
text.nite.lede: The gym closes. The habit does not. Take a shot at the night court — every make gets logged, the same way your reps do.
text.nite.trust: Grab the ball, pull it back, let it fly. A make sends you straight to booking.
